newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to raise capital adequacy requirements.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to raise capital adequacy requirements.

text.p: The Argentine Central Bank announced Thursday that capital adequacy requirements for the country's banking system would increase from the current 17 percent to 20 percent between March 1997 and March 1998.

The increase in the liquidity requirement on deposits of up to three months begins with a hike up to 18 percent from March next year, followed by a further one percentage point in September to 19 percent and another to 20 percent in March of the following year.

The Central Bank said in a statement it was also raising the liquidity requirement on deposits of up to a year to 10 percent by March 1998 from the current 7.0 percent. Deposits of over a year carry no liquidity requirement.

The bank underlined these requirements' role "permitting institutions to avoid risks of a liquidity crisis in the system" and said credit agencies took such things into account when awarding credit ratings.
"These measures will help reduce our risk rating by making the system more solid," it said.
